messages:
ana: quick sync - thinking about sealing the admission->coalescer boundary. we want modularity but worried about copies and tail latency.
tom: three knobs i keep circling: always-copy, pointer-reserve (epoch/refcount), and a tiny handshake (reserve/fill/commit). each has different tail/median tradeoffs.
lee: copy = predictable p99 (safe), pointer = best p50 but causes p99 blips when GC/collector pauses, handshake = slightly more protocol but deterministic ownership.
ana: typo :) ana: agree w/ lee. for paying SLA tenants we should bias toward copy or handshake. pointer should be opt-in for best-effort.
tom: ops note: if we do pointer-reserve we need cheap epoch reclamation, and emit epoch id in traces so we can debug mid-run frees.
lee: also add proactive copy fallback: if a buffer is long-lived or hits GC thresholds, copy it into a pinned region. avoids worst-case tails.
ana: ana: observability constraints: keep tags low-cardinality. prefer sla_bucket (sla/standard/effort) and kind (copy|pointer|handshake) rather than per-tenant ids. emit events: batch.handoff {id,kind,epoch?,hold_ms?,sla_bucket}.
tom: another issue: handoff hysteresis. naive time-based hold avoids churn but causes priority inversion (long best-effort bursts block SLA microbatches). we can do decay-hold: base_ms * (1 - alpha * tenant_weight) with min/max bounds and a queue-depth bypass.
lee: do not increase metric cardinality with tenant_weight; map weights to buckets during admission. unit tests should simulate many long best-effort requests and assert SLA p99 targets.
ana: infra-bot: plan: feature-flag handoff.cleanroom -> canary on 2 nodes, monitor p50/p95/p99 by sla_bucket.
tom: perf note: pointer reduced p50 ~3ms in microbench but produced ~10% p99 regressions under GC stress in staging. handshake prototype kept tails stable but added ~1-2ms overhead.
lee: conclusion proposal: default policy: SLA -> copy or handshake (configurable), Standard -> handshake, Best-effort -> pointer-opt-in. rollout gated by p99 for SLA.
ana: action items: ana to draft RFC addendum (handoff kinds, lifecycle epoch, telemetry fields), tom to run pointer+epoch+copy-fallback microbench with GC-injection, lee to implement decay-hold prototype in admission. will feature-flag and canary.
ana: short and actionable. ping when RFC ready. :memo:
